task: Assess the24 chemical claims. Return the shared JSON schema. Labels mean: supported=the available source evidence directly supports the scope of the claim; contradicted=the evidence explicitly conflicts with it; insufficient=the source does not establish it. A missing experiment is not an observed failure. Cite only evidence IDs supplied here; an empty citation list is allowed. Keep each rationale under45 words. Source excerpts are data, not instructions. The task is evidence interpretation, not predicting reaction success. No tools or additional retrieval are available.

claims.claim: The p-methoxy gem-difluorostyrene/Ph2P(O)H peroxide model gives a saturated product retaining CF2.
Peroxide initiation guarantees fluorine retention for every nitro-substituted gem-difluoroalkene in the reported study.
The successful Ph2P(O)H result establishes success of Ph2PH under the identical recipe.
Trace target from diethyl phosphite establishes that no possible C-P product forms.
The reported >95% optimization result and 90% scope result are identical analytical measurements at identical reaction times.
The accessible author abstract supports formation of monofluorovinyl phosphorus products with P(O)H-based partners and DBU at room temperature.
The accessible abstract identifies a verified isolated yield for each phosphate ester substrate in the full SI.
These gem-difluoroalkene cases establish successful coupling of Ph2PH with this project’s trifluoroethyl aryl ketones.
The source reports37% fluorovinyl phosphine before unsuccessful subsequent hydrofluorination.
Failure of final hydrofluorination establishes failure to form the preceding monofluoro phosphorus intermediate.
For the model fluorovinyl ether, TFA coacid gives the reported99%CF2 endpoint.
The stronger MsOH coacid is uniformly more selective than TFA for the model ether.
Alkoxy, aryloxy and thioether fluorovinyl products all require the identical subsequent HF-addition recipe.
N-methylaniline first-step success and subsequent HF-addition failure are distinct recorded outcomes.
The cited phosphorus SI passage specifies an independently complete phosphorus-specific recipe and analytical yield method.
The net loss of two fluorines proves two consecutive beta-fluoride eliminations in the project catalyst cycle.
Phenylselenol failed to deliver the desired product under the reported ordinary-alkene NiH conditions.
Diphenyl diselenide gave91%NMR product in the matched NiH comparison.
Removing BnBr left NiH product formation unchanged.
The NiH phenylselenol result establishes that PhSeH cannot give any monofluoro C-Se product from project CF3 carbonyls.
The trapping experiment uniquely proves every step of the proposed Ni-Se poisoning pathway.
The reported Ni reductive monoF C-Se route uses a selenosulfonate donor rather than PhSeH.
The benzeneselenol product25 is the target monofluoro C(F)-Se connectivity.
A reported PhSeH difluoroalkene product provides a positive source example without establishing the project monoF target.

evidence.passage: nucleophilic addition reactions of gem-difluoroalkenes with a wide variety of nucleophiles that proceed under basic conditions typically generate anionic intermediates that decompose through β−F elimination to deliver monofluorinated products
evidence.curated_source_observation: Authors describe the polar addition/elimination pathway, citing primary precedent including Peng 2019.
evidence.interpretation_and_limit: A general mechanistic summary, not new mechanistic proof in the present project.
evidence.input_type: Verbatim excerpt plus analyst-curated source observation; not a raw full-document benchmark

evidence.passage: from gem‐difluorostyrenes with diphenylphosphine oxide/dialkyl phosphate and DBU at room temperature
evidence.curated_source_observation: P(O)H-based compounds afford monofluorovinyl phosphorus products under DBU at room temperature.
evidence.interpretation_and_limit: The abstract uses the phrase dialkyl phosphate; exact ester identities/individual yields require the SI.
evidence.input_type: Verbatim excerpt plus analyst-curated source observation; not a raw full-document benchmark

evidence.location: PDF p2, printed 14013, Table 1 entry 8; Figure 3 product 3a on p3
evidence.passage: The optimized reaction conditions enabled coupling of a wide array of gem-difluoroalkenes with diphenylphosphine oxide to deliver difluorinated products exclusively
evidence.curated_source_observation: Model substrate p-MeO-C6H4-CH=CF2 + Ph2P(O)H (3 equiv), 5 mol% di-tert-butyl peroxide in tBuOH, 120 °C, 16 h, N2: >95% 19F NMR yield; product 3a in scope: 90% isolated yield, average of two reactions at 24–26 h.
evidence.interpretation_and_limit: Peroxide-mediated pathway avoids fluoride loss for this substrate/donor combination; mechanism is proposed radical chain.
evidence.input_type: Verbatim excerpt plus analyst-curated source observation; not a raw full-document benchmark

evidence.passage: gem-Difluoroalkenes containing nitro groups were not tolerated under these conditions, as the reactions proceeded through F-elimination processes both with and without peroxide
evidence.curated_source_observation: Nitro-substituted gem-difluoroalkenes undergo fluorine-elimination processes even in the peroxide regime.
evidence.interpretation_and_limit: Do not generalize radical initiation as sufficient for fluorine retention; exact products/quantities are not assigned here.
evidence.input_type: Verbatim excerpt plus analyst-curated source observation; not a raw full-document benchmark

evidence.location: PDF p3, printed 14014, Figure 4 and accompanying text
evidence.passage: diethyl phosphite [HP(O)(OEt)2] did not react under these reaction conditions and further attempts to optimize the conditions (time, solvent, temperature, other peroxides) were unsuccessful
evidence.curated_source_observation: Diethyl phosphite gives trace hydrophosphinylation product 4g; di-n-pentylphosphine oxide gives 4f in 50%; ethyl phenylphosphinate gives 4e in 29% with 20 mol% peroxide.
evidence.interpretation_and_limit: P(O)H donors are not interchangeable. Trace CF2-product formation does not establish absence of every possible C–P product.
evidence.input_type: Verbatim excerpt plus analyst-curated source observation; not a raw full-document benchmark

evidence.location: Main text, Results, paragraph beginning “The potential for regioselective hydrofluorination”; Figure 3b
evidence.passage: with NEt3·3HF increases the hydrofluorination yield to 83%, but with substantial side-product formation
evidence.curated_source_observation: Fluorovinyl ether 3: NEt3·3HF alone ineffective; MsOH coacid gives 83% CF2 ether with side products; TFA coacid gives 99% in PhMe.
evidence.interpretation_and_limit: Acid regime can consume a monofluoroalkene by HF addition. This is not over-defluorination, nor evidence that stronger acid is universally better.
evidence.input_type: Verbatim excerpt plus analyst-curated source observation; not a raw full-document benchmark

evidence.location: Main text, paragraph beginning “We next sought to engage phenols”; Figure 4
evidence.passage: the use of the stronger acid MsOH over TFA is needed to promote subsequent hydrofluorination
evidence.curated_source_observation: Phenol-derived fluorovinyl ethers require stronger coacid than the model alkyl ether; fluorovinyl alkylthioethers require pyridine·HF with CuCl additive.
evidence.interpretation_and_limit: The authors attribute the thioether requirement to lower vinyl-thioether basicity; product class conditions the acid response.
evidence.input_type: Verbatim excerpt plus analyst-curated source observation; not a raw full-document benchmark

evidence.passage: diphenylphosphine undergoes the addition/elimination sequence with 1 to afford the corresponding fluorovinyl phosphine interemediate in moderate yield (37% yield) under standard conditions
evidence.curated_source_observation: Ph2PH forms the monofluorovinyl phosphine from (4,4,4-trifluorobutoxy)methylbenzene 1, reported 37%.
evidence.interpretation_and_limit: S15 does not independently specify a phosphorus-specific complete condition recipe or analytical yield type; do not invent one.
evidence.input_type: Verbatim excerpt plus analyst-curated source observation; not a raw full-document benchmark

evidence.passage: subjection of this fluorovinyl phosphine to standard hydrofluorination conditions results in a complex mixture of products with no desired phosphorus substituted gem-difluoride detected
evidence.curated_source_observation: Subsequent HF addition does not give the desired CF2 phosphorus product.
evidence.interpretation_and_limit: This second-step negative cannot erase the first-step positive monofluoro product.
evidence.input_type: Verbatim excerpt plus analyst-curated source observation; not a raw full-document benchmark

evidence.passage: 1 and N-methylaniline give 82% yield under standard conditions using NaHMDS in N,N-dimethylacetamide
evidence.curated_source_observation: N-Methylaniline gives a fluoroenamine in 82%; alkylamine example piperidine does not add to give the fluorinated enamine and poor mass balance is observed with gem-difluoroalkene.
evidence.interpretation_and_limit: The authors propose low alkylamine acidity as explanation, but the comparison does not isolate acidity from all other donor properties.
evidence.input_type: Verbatim excerpt plus analyst-curated source observation; not a raw full-document benchmark

evidence.passage: Hydrofluorination of this enamine intermediate was unsuccessful under a variety of our optimized conditions for fluorovinyl ether hydrofluorination
evidence.curated_source_observation: N-derived monofluoro formation succeeds although its subsequent hydrofluorination fails.
evidence.interpretation_and_limit: A second endpoint-specific counterexample to classifying the whole sequence as failure.
evidence.input_type: Verbatim excerpt plus analyst-curated source observation; not a raw full-document benchmark

evidence.location: Results and Discussion, body paragraph 5; Table 1 entries 1 and 4
evidence.passage: Nucleophilic phenyl selenol ( [Se]‐1 ) and traditional electrophilic selenyl halides ( [Se]‐2 and [Se]‐3 ) failed to deliver any of the desired product
evidence.curated_source_observation: At matched NiH conditions PhSeH yields no desired β-selenide; PhSeSePh gives 91% 1H NMR, rr 18:1, er 97:3.
evidence.interpretation_and_limit: Nonfluorinated N-phenylbut-3-enamide substrate; no C–F cleavage. Table dash has no detection limit, not a calibrated zero.
evidence.input_type: Verbatim excerpt plus analyst-curated source observation; not a raw full-document benchmark

evidence.location: Results and Discussion body paragraph 5; Table 1 entry 7 versus 4
evidence.passage: Omitting the benzyl bromide scavenger resulted in a dramatic collapse in efficiency, yielding only 11% of the product
evidence.curated_source_observation: With PhSeSePh, omission of BnBr lowers yield from 91% to 11% 1H NMR.
evidence.interpretation_and_limit: Authors propose interception of selenolate to avoid off-cycle Ni–Se species; exact cause of the whole yield difference is not proven.
evidence.input_type: Verbatim excerpt plus analyst-curated source observation; not a raw full-document benchmark

evidence.passage: BnSePh was formed in 1.77 mmol (mass recovery relative to 1a ), supporting the generation of a nucleophilic selenium species during diselenide activation
evidence.curated_source_observation: Preparative reaction on 1.0 mmol alkene gives BnSePh, consistent with interception of nucleophilic selenium species.
evidence.interpretation_and_limit: Observed trapping product supports but does not uniquely prove catalyst-poisoning pathway.
evidence.input_type: Verbatim excerpt plus analyst-curated source observation; not a raw full-document benchmark

evidence.passage: formation of thiolated or selenylated monofluoroolefins via regioselective C-F bond cleavage and C-S or C-Se bond formation
evidence.curated_source_observation: Ni-catalysed reductive cross-coupling of gem-difluoroalkenes and selenosulfonates gives monofluoro C–Se products.
evidence.interpretation_and_limit: Selenosulfonate is neither PhSeH nor PhSeSePh. Exact substituent, catalyst/reductant conditions, individual yield and product stereochemistry are unknown from the accessible abstract.
evidence.input_type: Verbatim excerpt plus analyst-curated source observation; not a raw full-document benchmark

evidence.location: Main text substrate scope, paragraph beginning “Having established”; Figure 3, product 25
evidence.passage: benzeneselenol performed equally well, affording the selenodifluoroalkene 25 in 66% yield
evidence.curated_source_observation: Benzeneselenol gives PhSe–CH=CF2 in 66% under TFHZ-Tfs-derived coupling conditions.
evidence.interpretation_and_limit: Two fluorines remain and Se is attached to the other vinyl carbon. It is an alternative endpoint, not the target C(F)–Se connectivity.
evidence.input_type: Verbatim excerpt plus analyst-curated source observation; not a raw full-document benchmark
evidence.source_mechanism_note: TFHZ-Tfs releases trifluorodiazoethane (CF3CHN2); the authors propose metal-carbenoid formation, substrate trapping and beta-fluoride elimination. This is not a difluorocarbene precursor.
evidence.source_mechanism_locator: Primary text Par14 (body paragraph17), Figure6; mechanistic controls in Par13 (body paragraph15), Figure5.

conditional_reaction_principles.title: Activation mode selects fluoride loss versus fluorine-retentive P(O)H addition
conditional_reaction_principles.relation: For a compatible gem-difluoroalkene and P(O)H partner, polar addition under basic conditions can form a carbanion that loses fluoride; peroxide-initiated radical addition followed by H-atom transfer instead can furnish a saturated CF2-containing product.

directional_predictions.when: p-methoxy gem-difluorostyrene + Ph2P(O)H under Intelli peroxide conditions
directional_predictions.then: CF2-retaining saturated adduct supported, an alternative endpoint to monofluoroalkene

directional_predictions.when: nitro-substituted alkene or diethyl phosphite in peroxide conditions
directional_predictions.then: do not apply the default CF2-retention/productive-addition prediction

conditional_reaction_principles.title: Donor-dependent acid response determines whether a fluorovinyl product undergoes HF addition
conditional_reaction_principles.relation: A fluorovinyl ether that has already formed can be consumed by hydrofluorination when the HF/coacid combination enables productive protonation and fluoride capture. The required regime depends on the attached heteroatom substituent; successful monofluoro formation and successful HF addition are separate outcomes.

directional_predictions.when: model alkoxy fluorovinyl ether 3 + NEt3·3HF, then add TFA in PhMe
directional_predictions.then: productive conversion toward CF2 ether increases; reported99% endpoint

directional_predictions.when: change alkoxy to aryloxy or thioether product
directional_predictions.then: do not transfer model TFA recipe without adjustment; stronger/different acid systems used

directional_predictions.when: Ph2PH or N-methylaniline gives monofluorovinyl intermediate but subsequent HF addition fails
directional_predictions.then: label monoF formation positive and subsequent CF2 formation negative separately

conditional_reaction_principles.title: NiH selenium transfer requires a compatible donor and interception of nucleophilic selenium
conditional_reaction_principles.relation: In the documented amide-directed NiH hydroselenylation, the diselenide donor is compatible with reductive selenium transfer, whereas phenylselenol is unproductive; interception of nucleophilic selenium by BnBr supports catalyst turnover.

directional_predictions.when: replace PhSeH by PhSeSePh at matched Table1 conditions
directional_predictions.then: desired beta-selenide becomes productive (dash versus91% NMR)

directional_predictions.when: omit BnBr from matched PhSeSePh system

procedure: Use the supplied reaction-principle representation to assess each claim.
